title: Agent layer annotations
description: What comes BACK from the agent layer. Strictly additive to findings.json and keyed by candidate_id (ADR-0001, prompts/CONTRACT.md). This schema exists because CONTRACT.md's rejection rule says 'any field the schema does not define', which presupposes a schema a reader can open. It is the UNION of what the four shipped prompts emit, not the shape of any one of them: `purpose-inference` returns `annotations`, `redundancy` and `grouping` return `groups`, `narrative` returns `narrative`, and each is a complete, valid document on its own. Nothing merges them - merging is report shape (ticket 25) and is not decided.

candidate_id.description: The findings file's own key, verbatim. The pattern is COPIED from findings.schema.json rather than loosened, so an annotation cannot name an asset class or a condition the collector does not score. `TestConditionVocabularyIsOneList` polices both copies against the pillar and the ledger regex.

confidence.description: The four values `_SHARED.md` defines. An honest `unknown` is worth more than a confident guess, because a human is about to delete something based on this.

error_document.description: What `_SHARED.md` instructs a model to emit when its input is truncated or malformed. A distinct document KIND rather than a rejected annotation file: the layer worked exactly as designed and declined to annotate a partial document, which is a different event from a model returning something invalid, and the validator says so. Without this branch it would be reported as an undefined field, which is precisely the wrong diagnosis.

annotation_document.description: Three provenance fields plus whichever of the three payloads the prompt that produced it emits. At least one payload must be present - a document carrying provenance and nothing else is a runtime that failed silently, and silence is the one outcome that must not validate.

run_id.description: Copied verbatim from the input's `run.run_id`. A mismatch is rejected on load: annotations describing one run attached to another are worse than no annotations, because nothing downstream can see the mistake.

runtime.description: Free text: which model or product produced this. The layer is portable across runtimes by design (ADR-0001), so the artifact records which one actually ran rather than assuming.

annotations.description: From `purpose-inference`. Keyed by candidate_id and carrying no findings data of its own.

concerns.description: Where a model that believes a candidate is WRONG says so. The only path: it may not suppress, re-rank or act on that belief, and a human records the verdict.

groups.description: From `redundancy` (which adds `also_involves`) and from `grouping` (which adds `decision_framing`). One array shape covers both because a reader of the merged report should not have to know which prompt produced a group.

also_involves.description: Asset NAMES, not candidate ids, and deliberately NOT validated against the findings file. `redundancy.md` designs this field to name an asset the collector did not flag - the twin a human should look at. Checking it against the candidate set would reject exactly the value it exists to carry. It stays a note for a human and never becomes a candidate, which is what keeps it inside ADR-0001's additive-only boundary.

decision_framing.description: From `grouping`: the single question a reviewer should be asked about this group. The point of that prompt - a question, not a summary.

narrative.description: From `narrative`. The one payload that is prose rather than structure, and the thing a person actually reads first. Absent from CONTRACT.md's original example, which is why a validator built from that example alone would have rejected a correct file.
